The '''2023–24 season''' was [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea Football Club]]'s [[List of Chelsea F.C. seasons|118th year in existence]] and 35th consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in England|English football]].

Prior to this season, former Chelsea [[Captain (association football)|captain]] [[César Azpilicueta]] left the club at the end of his contract after eleven consecutive seasons, signing for [[Atlético Madrid]] in his native Spain. [[Chelsea F.C. Development Squad and Academy|Chelsea academy]] graduate [[Reece James (footballer, born 1999)|Reece James]] replaced him as club captain before the new season opened in July.

Managed by [[Mauricio Pochettino]] in his first and only season at the club, Chelsea continued to perform below par during the first half of the campaign, vanishing any title hopes. Nevertheless, the club reached the [[2024 EFL Cup final|final of the EFL Cup]], finishing as runners-up to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], as well as the semi-finals of the FA Cup.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68860454|title=Manchester City 1–0 Chelsea: Bernardo Silva scores late winner as holders reach FA Cup final|work=BBC Sport|date=20 April 2024|access-date=20 April 2024}}</ref> Chelsea ultimately made a marked improvement during the second half of the season, with only one loss in their final fifteen league matches played from February to May. Subsequently, this led the club to finish in 6th place, securing an immediate return to European football for the next season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ck5k5l8x0npt|title=Chelsea 2–1 Bournemouth: Moises Caicedo scores goal from halfway line|work=BBC Sport|date=19 May 2024|access-date=19 May 2024}}</ref> Despite the improvement in form in the latter half of the season, head coach Mauricio Pochettino left Chelsea by mutual consent on 21 May 2024 after less than one year and one season in charge.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-21 |title=Mauricio Pochettino leaves Chelsea after one season |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c1ww8xw8nywo |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
{{legend2|#CCFFCC|Win|border=1px solid #AAAAAA}}
{{legend2|#FFFFCC|Draw|border=1px solid #AAAAAA}}
{{legend2|#FFCCCC|Loss|border=1px solid #AAAAAA}}
{{legend2|#FFFFFF|Fixtures|border=1px solid #AAAAAA}}

Chelsea announced a tour of the [[United States]] to take part in the [[Premier League Summer Series]] pre-season tournament with matches against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]], [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] and [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea heading to USA for Premier League Summer Series |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/chelsea-heading-to-usa-for-premier-league-summer-series |access-date=13 April 2023 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=11 April 2023}}</ref> Prior to the Premier League Summer Series the Blues confirmed a pre-season fixture against [[Wrexham A.F.C.|Wrexham]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea to meet Wrexham in North Carolina pre-season fixture |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/chelsea-to-meet-wrexham-in-north-carolina-pre-season-fixture |access-date=20 April 2023 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=20 April 2023}}</ref> It was later announced that Chelsea's last game of their America tour would see them face German opposition [[Borussia Dortmund]] on 2 August.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea to play Borussia Dortmund in Chicago |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/chelsea-to-play-borussia-dortmund-in-chicago |access-date=1 May 2023 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=30 April 2023}}</ref>
